items.title: Mexico to send Cuba humanitarian aid despite Trump pressure

featured_image.name: Mexico's Sheinbaum pledges to send humanitarian aid to Cuba ...

items.description:
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced Sunday that her government will send humanitarian aid to Cuba this week, including food, medicine, and basic supplies, directly contradicting President Donald Trump's claim that Mexico had complied with his request to halt oil shipments to the Caribbean island.

Speaking at an official event in the northern state of Sonora, Sheinbaum said the assistance would be coordinated by the Secretary of the Navy and aimed at alleviating shortages facing Cuban families, hospitals, and essential services. She stated emphatically that she never discussed Cuban affairs in her phone conversation with Trump on Thursday, adding that her government seeks to "diplomatically solve everything related to the oil shipments for humanitarian reasons".[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Japan's factory activity hits 3-year high as China's data diverges

featured_image.name: Japan's factory activity growth hits near 3-1/2-year peak, PMI shows

items.description:
Japan's manufacturing sector registered its strongest expansion in more than three years in January, while China's factory activity painted a mixed picture as official data showed contraction even as a private survey pointed to modest growth.

The S&P Global Japan Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 51.5 in January from 50.0 in December, the highest reading since August 2022, according to data released Monday. The 50.0 threshold separates expansion from contraction.[1][2][3]

"Japan's manufacturing industry propelled itself back into growth territory at the start of 2026, with firms signalling the strongest upturns in output and new orders for nearly four years," said Annabel Fiddes, associate director of economics at S&P Global Market Intelligence.[4][1]

items.title: Ukraine imposes hourly power outages as harsh cold deepens energy crisis

featured_image.name: 'Normal life has disappeared': Russia's energy offensive plunges Ukraine into dark and bitter cold

items.description:
Ukraine announced that hourly power outage schedules and industrial consumption limits will take effect across all regions starting February 1-2, 2026, as the country reels from an energy crisis caused by relentless Russian attacks on its infrastructure during one of its harshest winters in recent memory.

The restrictions, announced by Ukrenergo, Ukraine's state-owned grid operator, come as temperatures in parts of the country are forecast to plunge as low as minus 30 degrees Celsius over the coming days. The schedules will apply to all categories of consumers from midnight to midnight, with residents advised to check local energy provider websites for specific outage times in their regions.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran's top diplomat says nuclear deal achievable amid US standoff

featured_image.name: Turkey's Foreign Minister Meets His Iranian Counterpart As Regional Tensions Rise

items.description:
Iran's top diplomat expressed confidence Sunday that a nuclear deal with the United States remains achievable even as both nations inch toward potential military confrontation, highlighting a volatile standoff defined by simultaneous diplomacy and displays of force.

In an interview with CNN, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he believes Tehran can reach an agreement with Washington on its nuclear program—but only if trust can be rebuilt. "Unfortunately, we have lost our trust in the US as a negotiating partner," Araghchi told the network, while noting that "fruitful" mediation by regional partners is helping advance discussions.[1][2][3]

His remarks came the same day Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei issued his sharpest warning yet to Washington, declaring that any American military strike would ignite "a regional war" across the Middle East.[4][5][6]

items.title: Iran's Khamenei warns US attack would trigger regional war

featured_image.name: Tehran warns of regional conflict if US attacks Iran

items.description:
Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei issued his most direct warning to the United States on Sunday, declaring that any American military strike would escalate into a broader conflict engulfing the Middle East.

"The Americans should know that if they start a war, this time it will be a regional war," Khamenei said, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency. The 86-year-old leader addressed a gathering in Tehran ahead of the anniversary of the 1979 Islamic Revolution, dismissing US military deployments as familiar posturing that would not intimidate Iranians.[1][2][3]

The previously unreported meeting between US General Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and Israeli Defense Forces Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir comes as both nations coordinate potential military planning while President Donald Trump weighs strikes against the Islamic Republic.[1][2]

items.title: Zelenskyy confirms Ukraine-Russia talks for Feb. 4-5 in Abu Dhabi

featured_image.name: Zelenskyy says energy ceasefire in Ukraine discussed at Abu ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced on Sunday that a new round of U.S.-brokered trilateral peace talks between Ukraine and Russia will take place in Abu Dhabi on February 4-5, with Kyiv ready for a "substantive discussion" on ending the nearly four-year war.

"Our negotiating team has just delivered a report. The dates for the next trilateral meetings have been set – February 4 and 5 in Abu Dhabi," Zelenskyy wrote on X. "Ukraine is ready for a substantive discussion, and we are interested in ensuring that the outcome brings us closer to a real and dignified end to the war."[1][2][3]

items.title: Pentagon delays Iran strikes to bolster Mideast air defenses

featured_image.name: US deploying THAAD missile defence system, troops to Israel

items.description:
The Pentagon is holding off on potential military action against Iran while it deploys additional air defense systems across the Middle East, U.S. officials told The Wall Street Journal on Sunday, as Washington prepares for the possibility of a broader conflict with Tehran.

While President Donald Trump's promised "armada," spearheaded by the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group, has arrived in the Arabian Sea, officials say a comprehensive offensive would require robust defensive coverage to protect American forces, Israel, and Arab allies from Iranian retaliation.

items.title: Musk says China's power output will triple US within a year

featured_image.name: Musk Slams US Solar Tariffs as Barrier to America's Power Needs at ...

items.description:
Elon Musk sounded the alarm on China's energy dominance late last week, predicting that the country's electricity generation will soon exceed that of the United States by a factor of three, driven by a rapid expansion in solar power.

"China electricity generation is still growing super fast, with solar being the largest incremental contributor, and will exceed America by a factor of 3X either this year or next," Musk wrote on X on January 31. The Tesla and SpaceX CEO was responding to a report highlighting that China accounted for 33.2 percent of global electricity generation in 2025—more than double the US share of roughly 14.2 percent.[1][2][3]
